title: XLOOKUP: the modern lookup (and its catch)
concept:
`XLOOKUP` fixes VLOOKUP's three weak spots. You point at the **search column** and the **return column** separately, so there's no column counting, and the return column can be on **either side**. It's an **exact match by default**. And it has a built-in **"if not found"** result.

`=XLOOKUP(C2,$J$2:$J$15,$K$2:$K$15)` returns the name for O1001's product ({{=XLOOKUP(C2,$J$2:$J$15,$K$2:$K$15)}}).
`=XLOOKUP("Standing Desk",$K$2:$K$15,$J$2:$J$15)` looks **left**: name → ID ({{=XLOOKUP("Standing Desk",$K$2:$K$15,$J$2:$J$15)}}).

> [!warn] **Version check before the test.** XLOOKUP only exists in **Excel 365, Excel 2021 and later, and Google Sheets**. In Excel 2016 or 2019 it's an unknown function and gives **#NAME?**. Ask which version the test uses, and keep VLOOKUP and INDEX/MATCH ready. This app's console runs XLOOKUP so you can learn it, but your test machine might not.

args.name: lookup_array
args.desc: the one column to search, e.g. `$J$2:$J$15`

args.name: return_array
args.desc: the column to return from, the same height, on either side

args.name: if_not_found
args.desc: optional: what to show instead of #N/A, e.g. `"Not found"`

worked.prompt: Return the product name for order O1001 (row 2) with XLOOKUP.
worked.explain: Search C2 ({{=C2}}) down the ID column, return from the name column in the same position: **{{=XLOOKUP(C2,$J$2:$J$15,$K$2:$K$15)}}**. Same answer as the VLOOKUP, with nothing to count.

mistakes: Search and return columns of different heights (`$J$2:$J$15` with `$K$2:$K$16`). Keep them the same size.
Relying on XLOOKUP in a test on Excel 2016/2019: #NAME?. Check the version first.
Passing a whole table as the return array when you meant one column.

drills.ask: With **XLOOKUP**, return the list price of the product on order O1003 (row 4).
Which **ProductID** belongs to "LED Desk Lamp"? (The ID column is to the *left* of the names.)
drills.hint: Search the names (`$K$2:$K$15`) and return from the IDs (`$J$2:$J$15`). XLOOKUP doesn't mind which side.

drills.ask: Order O1141 (row 142) uses a product that isn't in the price list yet. Return its product name with XLOOKUP, showing `"Not in price list"` instead of #N/A.
drills.hint: Use XLOOKUP's 4th argument, if_not_found: `"Not in price list"`.

drills.ask: What's the **RepID** of the rep on order O1001 (row 2)? Rep names are in `Q2:Q8`, IDs to their left in `P2:P8`.
drills.hint: Search E2's name in the rep names, return from the RepIDs.

questions.prompt: Your XLOOKUP works at home, but the test laptop runs Excel 2016 and shows #NAME?. Why?
options: XLOOKUP doesn't exist before Excel 2021/365, so Excel doesn't recognise the name
Excel 2016 needs FALSE at the end
questions.explain: #NAME? means Excel doesn't know the function. Fall back to VLOOKUP or INDEX/MATCH.

questions.prompt: By default, is XLOOKUP an exact or an approximate match?
questions.explain: Exact by default, unlike VLOOKUP, which is approximate when the 4th argument is left out.
P999 isn't in the list, so XLOOKUP returns the if_not_found value.

claimAfter: I can look up in any direction with XLOOKUP, with a built-in 'not found' result, and I know which Excel versions have it.
notYet: XLOOKUP's match_mode and search_mode options (approximate, wildcards, last-to-first). Rarely needed in tests.
